segments.text_original:
Fiscal Deficit to GSDP %
Note – The average fiscal deficit to GSDP ratio was 4.08% during the period of the YSRCP Government and the same during the first year of the TDP alliance Government has increased to 5.12%.

During the YSRCP Government, the huge fiscal deficit to GSDP ratio is owing to the economic disruptions caused by the outbreak of the Covid-19 pandemic that necessitated higher borrowings owing to lower Government revenues and the need for higher expenditure in crucial sectors.

The Fiscal Deficit to GSDP ratio in FY 2024-25 is higher that during any previous financial year with an exception of FY 2020-21, the year of the outbreak of the Covid-19 pandemic, during which there were severe economic disruptions.
Source – CAG and MOSPI

Revenue Deficit to GSDP %
Note – The average revenue deficit to GSDP ratio was 2.65% during the period of the YSRCP Government and the same during the first year of the TDP alliance Government has increased to 3.61%.

This very clearly demonstrates that, during the first year of the TDP alliance, there was an increased dependence on borrowings for revenue expenditure.
Source – CAG and MOSPI

segments.text_original:
Capital expenditure
Note – During the period of the YSRCP Government between 2019-24, 33.25% of the borrowings were utilized for Capital Expenditure. Despite this, we were criticized by the then opposition TDP party saying that the YSRCP Government was irresponsibly borrowing and not utilizing the borrowing for productive expenditure. 

But now during the first year of the TDP alliance Government, only 23.49% of the borrowings were utilized for capital expenditure.
Source – CAG and MOSPI

segments.text_original:
State Government revenues growth during April and May 2025
Source – CAG Monthly Key Indicators
The State GST revenues for the first two months of this financial year has demonstrated a year-on-year contraction to the tune of 9.89%.

Even if all the categories of State Government’s revenues are taken into consideration, Quite contrary to what the TDP Government had suggested, the figures released by the CAG indicate that the trend of economic sluggishness is more pronounced during the first two month of this financial year, with the tax revenues registering a decline of 0.11% and non-tax revenues registering a fall of 5.69% over previous year. If the State’s own revenues are taken into consideration, the fall during April and May 2025 when compared with April and May 2024 is 0.44%. 

This indeed presents a very gloomy picture about the State’s future.

segments.text_original:
FY 2024-25 fiscal performance
Source - CAG
Source – Union Government Accounts
From the provisional accounts for FY 2024-25 released by CAG, distressing facts had come to light with the State’s own revenues registering a year on year growth of only 3.08%, when the Central Government aggregate of Gross tax revenues and Non-tax revenues registered a year-on-year growth of 12.04% during 2024-25.

It is also pertinent to mention that during 2024-25, the revenue receipts on account of license fee under the new liquor policy is around 1,800 crores. This is neither a recurring item nor does it reflect consumption, therefore, if this amount is removed while making a comparison between the two years, then the year-on-year growth of State’s own revenues during FY 25 turns out to be only 1.15%.
